mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recover from their current troughs, weekday foot traffic and nearby discretionary spending should lift RETAIL_REC within four weeks because commuting re-anchors shopping trips around employment corridors.
evidence_refs: series:WORKPLACES
series:TRANSIT
fact:WORKPLACES fell to -46.4 at t-1w then improved to -23.1 at t-0w
fact:TRANSIT fell to -48.6 at t-1w then improved to -34.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain near or below their t-1w lows yet RETAIL_REC still rises over the next 28 days, the commuting-to-retail mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A further weakening in WORKPLACES from the current level signals more home-based routines, which depresses spontaneous retail visits and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -30 on a weekly mean after t-0w
evidence_refs: series:WORKPLACES
fact:WORKPLACES averaged -23.1 at t-0w after -46.4 at t-1w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES drops below -30 and RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior four-week mean, the home-based substitution claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS relative to its recent slump indicates warmer-weather leisure substitution, and that outdoor social activity spills into nearby shopping trips, pushing RETAIL_REC up over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week from a negative weekly mean
evidence_refs: series:PARKS
fact:PARKS moved from -21.1 at t-2w to -11.9 at t-1w
failure_condition: If PARKS improves by at least 5 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not improve within the next 14 days, the spillover hypothesis is false.

mechanism_narrative: When both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain deeply suppressed, access friction and reduced weekday circulation constrain shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC stays below its recent average over the next four weeks.
